renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: impact_composition
  title: Calls by impact class
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of annotated variant calls and the ring splits them by the impact class SnpEff assigned to the most severe consequence. It answers how many calls could change a protein.
    How to read: most calls of a typical callset are MODIFIER (non-coding or downstream) and only a small share is HIGH or MODERATE. A ring with an unusually large HIGH share is worth checking against the callers and the filter status.
    Lines and annotations: the classes are SnpEff's own. HIGH is a disruptive effect such as a stop gained or a frameshift, MODERATE a non-disruptive one such as a missense, LOW a mostly harmless one and MODIFIER a mostly non-coding one.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/inputoutput/
  column: variant_key
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: impact
  caption: calls, by impact class

- component: card
  title: Allele fraction of calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average variant allele fraction over the calls in view, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers whether the calls look heterozygous, homozygous or mixed.
    How to read: a box centred near 0.5 with a tail towards 1 is the shape of a diploid germline callset. A box pushed towards low values points to mosaic or low-confidence calls, so check the filter status and the read depth.
  column: vaf
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: allele fraction, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Read depth of calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median read depth at the called positions, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how much evidence stands behind a typical call.
    How to read: a low median or a wide box means many calls rest on few reads, so genotypes and allele fractions are less reliable. Compare the callsets before trusting a difference between callers.
  column: dp
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: read depth, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Most frequent consequences
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of annotated calls and the bars rank the consequence terms that account for most of them. It answers what kind of effect the callset mostly holds.
    How to read: terms such as downstream or intron variants lead on a whole-genome callset, while missense and synonymous variants lead among coding calls. A missing or surprising term can point to a filtered callset or a different annotation database.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/inputoutput/
  column: variant_key
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: consequence
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: the most frequent consequences

- component: advanced_viz
  id: annotated_vaf_against_depth
  title: Allele fraction against read depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a variant call: its read depth on the horizontal axis and its variant allele fraction on the vertical axis, coloured by SnpEff impact class. It answers whether the damaging calls rest on enough reads.
    How to read: calls at high depth cluster near 0.5 and 1, the heterozygous and homozygous alternate genotypes. Scattered values at low depth are expected sampling noise, and a HIGH or MODERATE call there deserves a manual look before follow-up.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn, because neither the callers nor SnpEff publish a depth or allele fraction rule for these calls.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Read depth
    y_title: Variant allele fraction
    legend_pos: right
  roles:
    x: dp
    y: vaf
    label: hgvs_p
    color: impact

- component: advanced_viz
  id: annotated_rainfall
  title: Calls along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a variant call placed at its chromosome position, with its variant allele fraction on the vertical axis and its colour set by impact class. It answers where the calls cluster along the genome and which regions hold the damaging ones.
    How to read: dense bands of points mark gene-rich or highly variable regions, and gaps mark regions without calls (centromeres, low mappability). A tight cluster of HIGH calls in one region is worth a look in the gene tiles.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the 95th percentile of the allele fractions in this table, a data-defined reference and not a published cut-off.
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_kind: Variant allele fraction
    color_by_columns:
    - impact
    - caller
    default_color_by: impact
    top_n_labels: 0
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chrom
    pos: pos
    score: vaf
    feature: gene

- component: figure
  title: Distribution of allele fractions
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the variant calls in an allele fraction bin, split by impact class. It answers how the genotypes spread and whether the damaging calls follow the same pattern as the rest.
    How to read: peaks near 0.5 and 1 are the heterozygous and homozygous alternate genotypes of a germline callset. A different shape in the HIGH class than in MODIFIER suggests artefacts concentrated in damaging calls.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: vaf
    color: impact
    labels:
      vaf: Variant allele fraction
      impact: Impact class

- component: table
  title: Annotated variant calls
  description: |-
    Each row is one annotated variant call with its locus, alleles, quality, filter status, genotype, depth, allele fraction, gene and SnpEff consequence. It answers the exact detail behind every other tile.
    How to read: sort by impact class or filter by gene to review the damaging calls, and check depth and filter status before relying on one.

- component: figure
  id: composition_bars
  title: Annotation counts by category
  description: |-
    Each bar is a category of the selected SnpEff summary section (an impact class, a consequence term, a genomic region, a variant type or a zygosity class), with its count, grouped by caller. It answers what kind of variants each callset holds.
    How to read: pick a section with the filter. Compare the callers within a category, and expect a few categories to dominate. A caller whose bars differ in shape from the others calls a different kind of variant.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/outputsummary/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: category
    y: count
    color: caller
    barmode: group
    labels:
      category: Category
      count: Count
      caller: Caller

- component: card
  title: Total count in the section
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of the counts in the selected section and the ring splits it by category. It answers whether one category dominates the section.
    How to read: pick a section with the filter first, because totals of different sections (variants, effects, regions) are not comparable. A ring held by one or two categories is the normal shape of an annotation summary.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/outputsummary/
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: category
  caption: share of each category

- component: card
  title: Largest share of a category
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest percentage any single category holds in its section, and the histogram shows how the percentages are distributed. It answers how concentrated the section is.
    How to read: a histogram piled near zero with a long tail is the usual shape, with many small categories and a few large ones. The zygosity section carries no percentage, because SnpEff reports counts only there.
  column: percent
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share per category

- component: table
  title: Summary sections table
  description: |-
    Each row is one category of one SnpEff summary section for a callset, with its count and percentage. It answers the exact numbers behind the bars and rings.
    How to read: filter by section and sort by count to list the dominant categories.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: burden_matrix
  title: Gene burden by callset
  description: |-
    Each cell is the number of coding variants SnpEff assigned to a gene (row) in a callset (column), a sample called by one caller. It answers which genes carry the most variants and whether the callsets agree on them.
    How to read: columns that cluster together call similar variants, so if the callers separate more than the sequencing depths do, the caller matters more than the data. A row that is dark in every column is a robust high-burden gene, and a row dark in one column only is a call to inspect.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/outputsummary/
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: gene_name

- component: table
  title: Gene burden table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene with its variant count in every callset. It answers the exact numbers behind the heatmap cells.
    How to read: sort a callset column to rank the genes, and compare across columns to spot a caller that misses a gene.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: caller_gene_overlap
  title: Gene overlap between callers
  description: |-
    Each bar is a combination of callers and counts the genes that exactly those callers report with at least one HIGH or MODERATE variant, coloured by how many callers are in the combination. It answers which callers agree that a gene is hit.
    How to read: a tall bar for all callers means a consensus gene list, and tall bars for a single caller point to calls only that caller makes. The overlap is by gene, so it is robust to different representations of the same variant.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/inputoutput/
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: table
  title: Gene membership by caller
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene with a 1 or 0 per caller for a HIGH or MODERATE variant. It answers which callers report a given gene.
    How to read: filter on one caller column to list the genes only it reports.

- component: card
  id: gene_burden_top
  title: Variants concentrated in a few genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of variants SnpEff assigned to genes, and the strip shows the share held by the five genes with the most. It answers whether the burden is spread out or concentrated.
    How to read: large genes and repeat-rich genes lead on any callset, so a high concentration is normal. A single gene far above the rest on one caller only points to a calling artefact.
  column: n_variants
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: concentration
  breakdown_col: gene_name
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: share held by the top genes

- component: card
  title: High-impact variants by caller
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of HIGH-impact variants, such as stop gained or frameshift, and the bars rank the callers by how many each reports. It answers which caller finds the most disruptive variants.
    How to read: a caller far ahead of the rest may call more false positives, and one far behind may miss real ones. Open the gene overlap to see which genes they agree on.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/inputoutput/
  column: n_high
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: HIGH-impact variants, by caller

- component: card
  title: Coding variants per gene
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of coding variants per gene and callset, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how many coding variants a typical gene carries.
    How to read: most genes carry few or none and a handful carry hundreds, so the median sits low and the upper whisker is long. A median that differs between callers means they disagree on the coding variants of a typical gene.
  column: n_coding
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: coding variants per gene, with their spread

- component: figure
  title: Variants by gene biotype
  description: |-
    Each bar is a gene biotype with the number of variants SnpEff assigned to its genes, grouped by caller. It answers which kinds of genes hold the variants.
    How to read: protein coding genes lead on most callsets. A caller with a different split of biotypes than the others is calling in different regions of the genome.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/outputsummary/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: biotype
    y: n_variants
    color: caller
    barmode: group
    labels:
      biotype: Gene biotype
      n_variants: Variants
      caller: Caller

- component: table
  title: Per-gene variant burden table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one callset with its variants split by impact class (HIGH, MODERATE, LOW, MODIFIER) and its coding total. It answers the exact counts behind the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by the HIGH column to list the genes with the most disruptive variants.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gene_impact_grid
  title: Gene impact by callset
  description: |-
    Each cell is a gene (row) in a callset (column, a sample called by one caller), coloured by the most severe SnpEff impact class that gene carries there. It answers which genes carry damaging variants and which callers agree.
    How to read: on a germline run this is caller agreement, not a cohort mutation landscape. A gene coloured HIGH in every column is a robust finding, and a gene coloured in one column only is a call to inspect.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/inputoutput/
  kind: oncoplot
  config:
    top_genes: 30
    legend_position: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    gene: gene
    mutation_type: mutation_type

- component: table
  title: Gene impact table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one callset with its worst impact class and its variant count. It answers the exact values behind the grid.
    How to read: filter by impact class to list the genes with disruptive variants.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: coding_variant_needles
  title: Coding variants along proteins
  description: |-
    Each stem is a coding variant placed at its amino-acid position on a gene's protein, coloured by SnpEff impact class and sized by allele fraction. It answers where in the protein the variants fall.
    How to read: a cluster of stems in one stretch of the protein suggests a hotspot or a functional domain worth checking. Stems that several callers share are stacked at the same position, so compare them by caller before trusting an isolated one.
    Source: https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/snpeff/inputoutput/
  kind: lollipop
  config:
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    feature_id: gene
    position: aa_pos
    category: impact
    label: hgvs_p
    effect: vaf

- component: advanced_viz
  id: coding_variant_structure
  title: Variants on the protein structure
  description: |-
    Each marked residue on the 3D structure is a coding variant, coloured by impact class, on a structure fetched by gene symbol. It answers where the variants sit in space, not only along the sequence.
    How to read: variants that neighbour each other in 3D but not in sequence can belong to one functional site. A variant whose residue differs between the model and the annotation is listed as a mismatch, because SnpEff counts along a transcript and the model along another isoform.
  kind: molecule_3d
  roles:
    entity: gene
    gene: gene
    position: aa_pos
    ref_aa: ref_aa
    category: impact
    value: vaf
    label: hgvs_p

- component: card
  title: Genes with most coding variants
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of coding variants with a protein change and the bars rank the genes that carry most of them. It answers which proteins are the most altered.
    How to read: long genes lead the ranking, so compare the count with the gene length before reading biology into it.
  column: variant_key
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: the genes with the most coding variants

- component: table
  title: Coding variants table
  description: |-
    Each row is a coding variant with its gene, protein position, impact class, consequence, protein change and allele fraction. It answers the exact detail behind the lollipop and the structure.
    How to read: filter by gene to list its variants, or by impact class to list the damaging ones.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: callset_variant_overlap
  title: Variant overlap between callsets
  description: |-
    Each bar is a combination of callsets (a caller on a sample) and counts the PASS variants that exactly those callsets report, coloured by how many callsets are in the combination. It answers which calls a caller keeps that the others drop.
    How to read: a tall bar for all callsets is the consensus. Bars for one caller alone are its private calls, and for a deeper and a shallower sample of the same individual the gap measures sensitivity, not truth.
    Note: filtered calls are left out, because a caller does not claim them.
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: table
  title: Variant membership by callset
  description: |-
    Each row is a PASS variant with a 1 or 0 per callset. It answers which callsets report a given variant.
    How to read: filter on one callset column to list its private calls.
